q: The Cantor-Bendixson theorem for closed subsets of ℝ states that every closed set F can be written as F = P ∪ C where:
opts: P is open and C is closed
P is a perfect set (closed, no isolated points) and C is countable — F = P ∪ C (disjoint)
P is compact and C is the boundary
P and C are both closed and uncountable
exp: Cantor-Bendixson: every closed subset F of ℝ (or any Polish space) decomposes uniquely as F = P ∪ C with P perfect (closed, dense-in-itself) and C = F\P countable. The perfect set P is the Cantor-Bendixson kernel (P = F^{(α)} for some countable ordinal α).
